articles.title: Estados Unidos devolvem ao Líbano fragmentos de antigos sarcófagos saqueados | G1
articles.standfirst: Departamento de Justiça dos EUA afirma que benefícios econômicos, científicos e de segurança nacional do treinamento de IA superam os prejuízos alegados pelo jornal
articles.summary: Departamento de Justiça dos EUA afirma que benefícios econômicos, científicos e de segurança nacional do treinamento de IA superam os prejuízos alegados pelo jornal
articles.body:
Fragmento de sarcófago que será devolvido ao Líbano. — Foto: FBI/Divulgação

Os Estados Unidos anunciaram, nesta quinta-feira (3), a devolução ao Líbano de fragmentos de sarcófagos da época romana saqueados da cidade de Tiro e recuperados após uma investigação do FBI .

As peças decorativas de chumbo foram entregues na quarta-feira ao consulado libanês em Nova York antes de serem repatriadas, informou a embaixada americana.

Segundo o ministro da Cultura libanês, Ghassan Salame, os fragmentos foram encontrados durante escavações ilegais e apresentam características típicas dos antigos ateliês de sarcófagos de Tiro.

O comércio de antiguidades saqueadas é disseminado no Oriente Médio. Em 2017, três peças antigas já haviam sido devolvidas ao Líbano.

Salame destacou que Tiro é uma região "excepcionalmente rica em patrimônio arqueológico" e sofreu graves danos durante os recentes ataques israelenses. Em julho, a Unesco incluiu a cidade em sua lista de Patrimônio Mundial em Perigo.

articles.title: Semana de Arte do Rio terá mais de mil horas de programação cultural | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reúne mais de 150 projetos e 74 festivais em 12 dias; maioria das atividades será gratuita e atrações ocupam locais como Lapa, Praça XV, Cinelândia, Gamboa e Praça Tiradentes.
articles.summary: Evento reúne mais de 150 projetos e 74 festivais em 12 dias; maioria das atividades será gratuita e atrações ocupam locais como Lapa, Praça XV, Cinelândia, Gamboa e Praça Tiradente
articles.body:
O Centro do Rio vai receber uma grande programação cultural a partir do dia 18, com mais de mil horas de atividades ao longo de 12 dias. A Semana de Arte do Rio reúne mais de 150 projetos e 74 festivais espalhados por praças, ruas e prédios históricos da região. A maior parte das atrações será gratuita.

A programação completa foi divulgada nesta quinta-feira (3). A abertura oficial está marcada para os Arcos da Lapa, e a proposta é ocupar diferentes espaços do Centro com manifestações de arte e cultura.

“É uma semana de arte que olha para aquilo que nos faz Rio de Janeiro e aquilo que ainda vai nos fazer Rio de Janeiro. É uma plataforma para trazer curadores e colecionadores do mundo todo para verem o que o Rio produz de melhor”, afirmou o secretário municipal de Cultura, Lucas Padilha.

Praça XV, Cinelândia, Gamboa e Praça Tiradentes estão entre os locais que vão concentrar parte das atrações. Segundo a organização, a iniciativa busca aproximar o público dos espaços culturais e do patrimônio histórico da região.

Entre os destaques da programação está a apresentação da cantora Fafá de Belém, na Lapa, no dia 18. Na mesma data, Mart'nália se apresenta no Palácio Capanema.

No dia seguinte, o projeto Aquarius reúne o rapper Emicida, a sambista Leci Brandão e a Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira em uma programação que mistura rap, samba e música clássica.

A literatura também terá espaço com a Flup, a Festa Literária das Periferias. Já as artes visuais serão representadas pela 16ª edição da ArtRio, na Marina da Glória.

No Galpão da Ação da Cidadania, o público poderá assistir ao espetáculo “Senhora dos Afogados”, de Nelson Rodrigues. A montagem tem no elenco nomes como Leona Cavalli e Giulia Gam.

O Museu do Amanhã também terá uma programação especial durante o evento. O espaço funcionará em horário estendido, até as 19h — normalmente, o museu fecha às 18h.

Além disso, será inaugurada uma nova área pública de convivência, com uma nova cantina e atividades paralelas.

“A gente vai ter horário estendido, vamos estar aqui até as 19h. O museu normalmente fecha às 18h e vamos ter uma nova área pública, uma área de convivência, uma nova cantina que vai ter programação paralela no museu”, explicou Cristiano Vasconcelos, diretor executivo do Museu do Amanhã.

Segundo a Prefeitura do Rio, a Semana de Arte passa a integrar o calendário oficial da cidade e está prevista no planejamento estratégico municipal para os próximos anos.

A iniciativa também é apresentada como parte da estratégia de reforço do programa Reviver Centro, que busca estimular a ocupação e a revitalização da região central da cidade por meio de ações culturais, urbanas e econômicas.

articles.title: Hidrogel reduz irrigação de mudas durante calor intenso em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Hidrogel retém água no solo, reduz a necessidade de irrigação e aumenta a sobrevivência das mudas em áreas com altas temperaturas da capital.
articles.summary: O hidrogel agrícola reduz a irrigação em 50% e protege a arborização de Teresina contra o estresse hídrico durante o rigoroso período do B-R-O-Bró.
articles.body:
Mudas de árvores plantadas em Teresina passaram a receber este ano hidrogel no plantio. Com o recurso, a capital do Piauí, conhecida por registrar altas temperaturas principalmente no período do B-R-O-Bró, reforça a arborização com economia de água.

🌱 O hidrogel agrícola é um recurso que absorve água e nutrientes, e os libera aos poucos, evitando o estresse hídrico. Além disso, ele reduz a necessidade de rega em até 50%, aumentando a taxa de sobrevivência das plantas.

Em Teresina, as temperaturas podem ultrapassar os 40º C, principalmente entre os meses de setembro a novembro. O uso do hidrogel auxilia os órgãos municipais a realizar uma irrigação de forma calculada, sem prejudicar a vegetação.

Em entrevista à TV Clube , na quarta-feira (2), o assessor da Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente, Lívio Lacerda, contou que o projeto conta com a parceria de outros órgãos do munícipio para manter as plantas com a irrigação correta.

"Nesse período, as plantas tendem a sofrer um pouco mais. Com a escassez de água, com a secura, com toda essa situação que advém do B-R-O-Bró. (O hidrogel) tem uma ação tão somente de fortalecer e umidificar o solo, a ponto de que o solo consiga reter umidade por mais tempo, fazendo com que a gente faça um cronograma para atender toda a cidade", afirmou.

Teresina utiliza hidrogel para manter mudas e economizar água em período de seca — Foto: Montagem (TV Clube/Reprodução/Semam)

Segundo a Semam, o hidrogel é geralmente utilizado em lugares onde não há ponto de água instalado, como canteiros centrais de avenidas.

Lívio destaca que as avenidas Kennedy, Henry Wall de Carvalho, Frei Serafim, Nossa Senhora de Fátima, João XXIII e Dom Severino são as primeiras da capital a receberem esse tipo de plantio. Ele informa ainda que o projeto pode ser expandido para outras regiões de Teresina.

*Eduarda Barradas, estagiária sob supervisão de Ilanna Serena.

articles.title: Entre dunas e mar, Pitangui guarda um novo jeito de descansar | G1
articles.standfirst: Inaugurado em dezembro de 2025 na Praia de Pitangui, em Extremoz (RN), o resort do GR Group aposta em silêncio, mar calmo e serviço de alto padrão no litoral norte potiguar.
articles.summary: Inaugurado em dezembro de 2025 na Praia de Pitangui, em Extremoz (RN), o resort do GR Group aposta em silêncio, mar calmo e serviço de alto padrão no litoral norte potiguar
articles.body:
Entre dunas e mar, Pitangui guarda um novo jeito de descansar — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

O litoral norte do Rio Grande do Norte tem um ritmo próprio. Quem sai de Natal em direção a Extremoz vê a paisagem trocar a linha de prédios por dunas, coqueiros e faixas de areia clara. O mar fica mais calmo. O barulho diminui.

É nesse trecho que está a Praia de Pitangui, um dos endereços mais preservados da região. As águas são tranquilas. A poucos minutos dali, a Lagoa de Pitangui guarda água doce entre a vegetação. Mais ao sul, as Dunas de Genipabu recebem os passeios de buggy que viraram cartão-postal do estado.

Desde o fim de dezembro de 2025, esse cenário passou a contar com um novo endereço de hospedagem.

O Wyndham Natal Pitangui Praia foi inaugurado em dezembro de 2025, na Avenida Rocco Rosso, em Extremoz. O empreendimento tem operação hoteleira da rede Wyndham.

A estrutura reúne piscinas adulto e infantil, bar na piscina, sauna, fitness center, espaço kids, área de jogos e recepção 24 horas. Os quartos e suítes têm varanda privativa, smart TV e internet de alta velocidade, com vista para o mar, para a piscina ou para o pátio. Há acomodações acessíveis e berços sob solicitação.

O complexo inclui ainda o Pitangui Lagoa Park, a cerca de dois minutos da praia, junto à lagoa de água doce. Estacionamento gratuito, ar-condicionado, frigobar, elevador e equipe multilíngue completam a lista de comodidades.

A gastronomia fica a cargo do Restaurante Acquarela, sob o comando de chefs especializados. A proposta combina ingredientes frescos e sabores regionais com técnicas da culinária francesa. O café da manhã está incluso na diária e há serviço de quarto ao longo do dia.

O resort também recebe eventos corporativos, casamentos e celebrações, o que amplia o calendário do empreendimento para além da alta temporada de verão.

Extremoz fica a poucos quilômetros da capital e, por muito tempo, recebeu visitantes sobretudo em passeios de um dia. Um equipamento hoteleiro de alto padrão instalado na própria praia altera essa lógica, porque permite que o turista fique, e não apenas passe.

O estado combina praias de águas mornas, dunas e sol durante boa parte do ano. No litoral norte, esses atributos aparecem com menos densidade construída do que na orla da capital.

Essa é a leitura que o grupo faz do próprio investimento: Pitangui é onde o Brasil ainda é exclusivo. O resort não veio preencher a paisagem, veio oferecer tempo para contemplá-la!

O Wyndham Natal Pitangui Praia fica na Avenida Rocco Rosso, s/n, Praia de Pitangui, Extremoz (RN). Informações sobre acomodações, reservas e eventos estão no site wyndhamnatalpitangui.com . articles.title: Iran attacks US targets despite Trump threats
articles.summary: Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday, despite President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war...
articles.body:
Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday, despite President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war.

The new clashes, which began with US raids on Sunday, deepen the ongoing impasse in the war, as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz and the US presses its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump said his military was prepared to attack Iran "any time we want" after extensive US bombardment of sites across the country left at least 19 Iranians dead between Tuesday and Wednesday.

Tehran has once again retaliated with strikes across the Middle East this week, saying it targeted US bases and forces in the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq's Kurdistan region.

Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned the United States on Wednesday that Iran had adopted a "new strategy" in the war that "will shatter your foundations".

Iran's pummelling of US military targets across the region came after a US attack that hit a wedding in the country's south, prompting fury from Tehran.

The Iranian Red Crescent said shrapnel from the missile attack in the coastal town of Kuhestak killed four people, including a child, and wounded more than 50.

The US military did not address the attack directly.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesman Tim Hawkins said "the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC", referring to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

Kuwait's army on Thursday said it was intercepting a missile and drone attack from Iran, with the Iranian army saying it hit "the Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait with missiles and drones".

Iran's army also said it struck Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, but the Gulf country reported no such attack.

Kuwait called the attacks "a direct threat to its security and stability, and the safety of its citizens and residents on its territory, and a grave breach of the rules of international law".

Aside from military action, Washington has vowed to choke Iran's economy, threatening to slap sanctions on its trade partners.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright pledged on Wednesday that a US plan for expanded sanctions targeting the Islamic republic's economic partners would deliver "absolutely maximum pressure".

Trump also suggested on Wednesday renaming the Strait of Hormuz, a major shipping lane that Tehran has effectively shut for six months, as "Trump Strait" -- although he implied later that he wasn't serious.

"Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???" the US president wrote on Truth Social.

Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf lashed out at Washington over the wedding attack, calling the United States "Satan".

"If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it's Satan," he posted on X.

Iranians meanwhile expressed dismay over the return to hostilities.

Hossein Moazami, 50, who is self-employed, called the attacks "truly distressing".

"I hope they all return to the negotiating table because the only people suffering from this are the Iranian people," he said. "The Americans are on the other side of the world and nothing happens to them."

A video shared by an Iranian government account showed debris and damage at what it said was the wedding site in Kuhestak following the US strike, with people heard screaming in the background.

"It is a very saddening incident," Ali Mallahi, father of the bride and owner of the building that was hit, said in a video carried by state TV.

"Thank God the casualties were not higher."

The war erupted on February 28 with US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed its supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

A fragile ceasefire collapsed in July after attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.

Israel's defence minister meanwhile said his country was prepared to respond "with great force" if attacked by Iran over the Jewish high holiday season, which begins in mid-September.

"For now, they are striking throughout the region except us," Israel Katz said.
authors: AFP bureaus in Tehran, Washington and Dubai

articles.title: Quote of the Day by Confucius: "By three methods we may learn wisdom, first, by reflection, which is noblest; second, by imitation, which is...."
articles.summary: More than 2,500 years after his death, Confucius’ ideas continue to shape the way millions of people think about education, family, leadership, morali.
articles.body: More than 2,500 years after his death, Confucius’ ideas continue to shape the way millions of people think about education, family, leadership, morality and human relationships. Confucius was born in ancient China at a time of political instability and social upheaval. He did not base his philosophy on sweeping theories about the universe. Rather, he was concerned with something much closer to the quotidian, of how human beings should act, how they should treat one another and construct a just society.Chinese Kong Fuzi, or “Master Kong” Confucius was born c. 551 BCE in the state of Lu (now Shandong province, China). Although his family was of the lesser nobility, his early life was troubled by financial difficulties. Confucius’ father died when he was young and Confucius had to work at many different jobs before becoming a teacher. Confucius believed that everyone who wanted to learn should be able to learn, at a time when education was largely reserved for the aristocracy. He taught students regardless of their social background and was said to be a demanding but influential teacher. In his approach to education he did not simply learn facts. He wanted his students to think, to question, to reflect and to grow in character. To Confucius, knowledge without moral character was incomplete.A teacher who changed the definition of wisdomConfucius lived in the Spring and Autumn period, when China was divided into competing states and traditional political and social structures were breaking down. He believed that many of society’s problems stemmed from a lack of morality and responsibility. His answer was not a revolution. It was self-betterment. A stable society begins with individuals knowing their responsibilities to other people, he said. A good ruler should lead by virtue, not by fear. Parents take care of their children, children respect their parents, friends are trustworthy and people act with honesty and consideration.One of the most important ideas he developed was ren, usually translated as “humaneness”, or “benevolence”, or compassion for fellow human beings. Another was li, a generic term for proper conduct, rites, manners and social duties. In these ideas he expressed his belief that a good society is built through everyday behaviour.Confucius also emphasised learning enormously. He did not think wisdom automatically came with age. The individual had to actively seek it out, review mistakes and be willing to get better. This made the teacher-student relationship the center of his philosophy. The right person wasn’t someone who thought they knew everything already, it was someone who was curious and willing to learn.His entry into politicsConfucius did not wish to remain simply a teacher. He also hoped to improve government with his ideas. Eventually he accepted administrative and political posts in the state of Lu, and became involved in efforts to restore order and good government. But rivalries and political differences thwarted his influence. Traditional accounts tell that he then went from state to state, trying to convince rulers to take a more ethical approach to leadership. His political career was not a success story of sweeping reforms as he had hoped. His political failure, in the end, did not diminish his influence.He returned to teaching and continued to study and pass on the traditions of ancient China. His teachings were preserved by his students, and later compiled into the Analects, a collection of conversations, observations and sayings attributed to Confucius and his disciples.Confucius died c. 479 BCE, but his intellectual journey was not over.The philosophy that lasted 2,500 yearsEventually, Confucianism became one of the major intellectual traditions in East Asia. Its influence spread across China, later to Korea, Japan and Vietnam. For centuries, Confucian ideas dominated Chinese education, government, and social life. His emphasis on scholarship and learning had a similar effect on the civil service examination systems that helped decide who could enter the government.Quote of the DayOne of the sayings attributed to Confucius offers a remarkably simple way of understanding how people become wiser: ‘There are three methods for acquiring wisdom: First, by reflection, which is the noblest; second, by imitation, which is the easiest; and third, by experience, which is the bitterest."The first method is that of reflection. Confucius thought that reflection was the highest form of learning, for it involves the stopping to think. We can learn not only from what happens to us but by examining our actions, decisions and beliefs. Thought creates an event to comprehend. A person can make a mistake, for instance, but the mistake in itself doesn’t create wisdom. And they ask me, why did I do that? And that's wisdom. What was I to do? What does this say about myself?This profound consideration of life is what makes reflection “the noblest” path. The second method is the easiest, according to Confucius, and that is imitation. Humans learn in a natural way through watching others. Children learn how to behave by watching their parents. A teacher teaches a student. Young professionals learn from senior colleagues. Sometimes we get better just by finding people we admire and trying to be like them.Imitation can therefore save us making all the mistakes ourselves. If we see someone being patient, brave, disciplined or kind we can learn from their example, without having to find out for ourselves through hard experience. But there’s a limit to imitation: we need to choose our models carefully. To copy blindly is not to be wise. The real value is in seeing admirable behaviour, understanding why it works, and then making it part of our own character.The third way is experience, and Confucius calls this the “bitterest”. This is probably the most recognisable form of learning . We often discover life lessons only after we’ve lived them. Failure can teach you resilience. “Loss can teach us gratitude.” Disappointment can show us who truly has our back. A wrong choice can show us things that no book could have explained better. Experience is a hard teacher because she gives the test first, the lesson afterward.But those lessons can also be all-consuming. So the three methods are in progression. We can learn from our own thoughts, we can learn from the wisdom of others, or we can wait for experience to teach us, sometimes painfully. The deeper message is that wisdom isn’t just a product of growing older. It is derived from listening.One may get older, but not likely wiser if they keep making the same mistake over and over again without learning from it. Another person can learn from looking at someone else’s choices and never make the same mistake.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Salman Khan's Panvel farmhouse has rice fields, horses and a garden: What makes the actor's country retreat unlike a typical celebrity home
articles.summary: Salman Khan’s Panvel farmhouse is no ordinary celebrity getaway. Spread across 150 acres and known as Arpita Farms after his sister, the place feels m.
articles.body: Salman Khan’s Panvel farmhouse is no ordinary celebrity getaway. Spread across 150 acres and known as Arpita Farms after his sister, the place feels more like a working countryside retreat than a flashy weekend pad. It has rice fields where the actor has planted saplings himself, stables for his horses, and gardens that grow vegetables and fruits for the family table.Valued at around Rs 80 crore, it sits in the quiet outskirts of Panvel, surrounded by greenery, mountains and waterbodies, offering a rare glimpse of how one of Bollywood’s biggest stars chooses to live when the cameras are off. What sets it apart is simple. Most star homes lean heavily on marble, gold and show. This one mixes comfort with real farm work, animal care and open land that the family actually uses.A living farm, not just a pretty backdropDuring the lockdown years, Salman spent long stretches at the farmhouse with family. Videos from the lockdown time show him driving a tractor, getting mud on his clothes and planting rice saplings alongside relatives and staff. The fields are not decorative. They form part of the daily rhythm of the property. Reports note that he grows potatoes, tomatoes, pumpkins and other vegetables without artificial fertilisers, often cooking them for guests.Orchards with different fruit trees add to the harvest. His father, Salim Khan, once said the produce is meant only for the family, not for sale. It is a quiet commitment to healthier food and a slower pace. That hands-on farming is what makes the place feel different from the typical celebrity estate where land is mostly for the view.Horses, stables and a soft spot for animalsSalman has long been known for his love of horses. The farmhouse has well-kept stables where the animals live and are cared for. He is often seen feeding them, riding or simply spending time nearby. Family members and visitors have shared moments of horse rides and quiet mornings around the stables.Beyond horses, the grounds are home to dogs, goats and other animals. Some accounts even mention space that functions like a small shelter. The open land lets the animals move freely, which fits the actor’s well-documented affection for creatures of all kinds. In a world where many luxury homes keep pets as accessories, here the animals are part of the everyday life of the place.Rustic comfort that still feels like homeInside, the design stays warm and grounded. Wooden flooring, large windows that pull in natural light, leather couches and earthy tones create a lived-in feel rather than a showroom. There are multiple bungalows on the property so the extended family can stay together comfortably.Outdoors, a swimming pool is framed by palm trees, lounge chairs and a serene Buddha statue, giving it a resort feel, but it maintains the countryside feel. And a fully equipped gym keeps the fitness-conscious actor healthy when he’s away from the city. Natural features add to the charm: walking trails, misty mountain views, a small river and even a cave-like area with a waterfall. articles.body: KOLKATA: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday warned schools that financial aid and other government support would be stopped if the mandatory singing of the full version of Vande Mataram during school prayers was not strictly followed.Addressing the annual programme of Vivekananda Vidya Bharati Vikas Parishad, an RSS-affiliated organisation, at Ramakrishna Mission in Kolkata's Golpark, Adhikari alleged that the state's education system had been "brought to the brink of destruction" under successive governments in the past.He said the current BJP dispensation was carrying out reforms to restore Indian culture, traditions and nationalist values in school education."A few people had objected to singing the complete rendition of Vande Mataram. I told them that government aid would stop. Then they budged, but only partially. They stood up, but did not move lips. Then I told them that lips must move as well," the CM said, sporting a smile.Adhikari claimed that English-language education was curtailed during the Left Front regime, while the TMC era had "distorted school curricula through appeasement politics".He said words such as 'maa', 'jal' and 'akash' in school curricula were deliberately replaced with 'amma', 'pani' and 'asmaan', respectively.He said the "subtle changes" were in contrast to the pedagogic ideas of stalwarts like Iswar Chandra Vidyasagar and Swami Vivekananda.The CM also accused the previous government of committing the "unforgivable crime" of banning the National Cadet Corps (NCC) in educational institutions."I met defence minister Rajnath Singh recently and made two requests: First, I urged him to build more Sainik Schools in the state, and second, I told him I will write to him seeking permission to make NCC mandatory in schools and colleges. I have already sent him that letter and received his assurance to do the needful," the CM said.Adhikari's remarks came amid continuing political disagreements in West Bengal over education policy, curriculum changes, teacher recruitment and the role of ideology in educational institutions."The people of West Bengal provide time when it comes to change and giving opportunities. They gave time to the Congress after Independence, gave sufficient opportunities to the subsequent United Front and Left Front governments, and for the last 15 years they had given time to the TMC," he said."But they also brought about the change in the state at the right time, else an Islamic education system of Bangladesh would have been replicated here," Adhikari said, referring to the state's political history.He claimed that if the education policy followed during the last decade of TMC rule had continued for some more time, "our values, our heritage, tradition, patriotism and nationalism were pushed to the brink of getting lost forever".Adhikari said people had brought about political change in the state at the "right time", arguing that reforms were needed to restore the education system and foster patriotism among young people.Claiming that the school education system during the previous TMC era contributed to "creating divisions among children", the CM said, "Scholarships from classes 5-8 were made available only to Muslim students while the opportunity was denied to students of other communities."He claimed that the syllabus referred to the removal of the Tata group from Singur but did not mention the contribution of Syama Prasad Mookerjee in the formation of West Bengal."The name of former state minister Partha Chatterjee, an accused in school recruitment scam, was included, while the names of freedom fighters such as Khudiram Bose and Matangini Hazra were difficult to find in textbooks," he alleged.Turning to the political debate surrounding the recent unrest at Jadavpur University and slogans relating to Kashmir and Palestine, the chief minister launched a scathing attack on dissident voices within the institution."Bengal is the land of Netaji and Shyamaprasad. Swami Vivekananda was born in Kolkata. And on this land you will say 'Kashmir maange azaadi'! There are no rallies when Pahalgam happens, but during Operation Sindoor, you say, stop the war. articles.title: In 1982, Ralph Lauren bought land around a century-old Colorado barn; decades later it had grown into a 17,000-acre ranch and wildlife preserve
articles.summary: US News: In 1982, Ralph Lauren came across an aging wooden barn beneath Colorado’s San Juan Mountains and immediately saw something others might have overlooke.
articles.body: In 1982, Ralph Lauren came across an aging wooden barn beneath Colorado’s San Juan Mountains and immediately saw something others might have overlooked. The nearly century-old Vance barn stood on land outside Ridgway, surrounded by mountain scenery and open meadows. Lauren and his wife, Ricky, fell in love with the property and began building what would eventually become the Double RL Ranch. What started with a historic barn and a relatively modest piece of land grew over the following decades into a sprawling 17,000-acre landscape combining family life, cattle ranching, wildlife habitat and Lauren’s enduring fascination with the American West. In its own account of the property, Ralph Lauren describes the ranch as both a home and an expression of a longstanding Western dream.The century-old barn that started Ralph Lauren’s Colorado dreamThe story of the Double RL Ranch begins with the Vance barn, built in 1905 by Thomas Vance at the base of Colorado’s San Juan Mountains. According to Ralph Lauren’s account, the enormous structure was designed to shelter dairy cattle through severe mountain winters and was constructed from lumber hand-cut from nearby forests. The barn eventually became recognisable to a much wider audience after appearing in Marlboro television commercials. Lauren first encountered it in 1982, when he and Ricky were searching for land in the American West. The couple had considered properties in Utah and Wyoming, but the Colorado landscape surrounding the barn captured their imagination. Lauren later recalled that seeing the mountains and the old structure gave him an immediate sense that the property was special.From neglected property to a carefully preserved ranchWhen Lauren acquired the land, the historic barn was no longer in pristine condition. Ralph Lauren’s feature explains that its floor, porch and hayloft required extensive renovation. The restoration was eventually completed in 2000, while new family and guest buildings were positioned carefully around the landscape. Lauren has described his reluctance to build extensively on the property because he valued the appearance of undisturbed land. Instead, homes were placed in low, inconspicuous locations and partially hidden among trees. The approach reflected a broader philosophy: the buildings were meant to belong to the landscape rather than overwhelm it. Over time, the ranch developed into a distinctive combination of historic architecture, family spaces and open Colorado country, while retaining the character that attracted Lauren to the property in the first place.A 17,000-acre working cattle operationThe Double RL Ranch eventually expanded to roughly 17,000 acres and remained a genuine working cattle operation rather than simply becoming a private retreat. Ralph Lauren’s own published material describes the property as a world-renowned cattle ranch, while another Ralph Lauren feature notes that around 800 Angus and South Devon steers and heifers graze across the ranch. Cowboys move the cattle between pastures on horseback, maintaining a distinctly traditional approach to ranch life. The operation also has a direct connection to Lauren’s businesses: the ranch has supplied beef to Ralph Lauren restaurants in New York and Chicago. This combination of livestock, working cowboys and expansive pastureland gives the property an agricultural purpose alongside its role as the Lauren family’s Colorado home.Where cattle country meets a wildlife preserveThe ranch's significance extends beyond cattle. Ralph Lauren describes the 17,000-acre property as a place where eagles, elk and deer can remain undisturbed among piñon pines and wild sunflowers. That coexistence between ranching and wildlife is central to the character of the Double RL Ranch. Rather than treating the landscape simply as a backdrop for a luxury home, the property has retained large areas of open habitat alongside its agricultural operations. The result is an unusual landscape where cattle grazing, wildlife and the Lauren family’s connection to the American West exist together. The restored Vance barn, meanwhile, remains a physical reminder of the land’s history, linking the ranch today with the working agricultural property Lauren first encountered more than four decades ago.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: This California town with 27 apartments and a local post office is still looking for a buyer. The price has come down to $5.9 million
articles.summary: US News: Campo, an entire town in California, just an hour away from San Diego, has been on sale for years. Now the price has hit its lowest as it did not get .
articles.body: Campo, an entire town in California, just an hour away from San Diego, has been on sale for years. Now the price has hit its lowest as it did not get any luck. The town has its own local post office, a border patrol facility, a church, a VFW (Veterans of Foreign Wars) post, 27 apartments and a hardware store. This isn't the first time Campo has hit the market. The town was listed in 2019 and again in 2024, when it was priced at $6.5 million before being taken off the market. Now it's again on the market with a price of $5,995,000.The current owner, John Ray, has owned the town for 22 years. According to 10News, Ray said he hasn't had the time to develop the property, and so far, it hasn't sold. The listing agent, Nick Hernandez, said the sale covers a specific portion of the area. "It's bringing in about forty thousand a month in current rents," Nick said.The parcels for sale are not considered historical land, according to Nick. But they sit within a town steeped in history as Campo was once home to a military base in World War II."The opportunity extends to revitalizing currently vacant buildings within the town, a move that could add substantial income by introducing new or enhanced services like gyms, laundromats, daycares, or community centers, directly responding to the desires and needs of the local population," reads the real estate listing.History of the townAccording to California Post, the location became prominent in 1885 when the Gaskill brothers constructed the fortress-like Campo Stone Store on-site using four-foot-thick walls to protect against border raids. During World War II, the area changed massively when the US Army absorbed the land to construct Camp Lockett, building a sprawling network of military barracks to garrison the legendary Buffalo Soldiers of the 10th and 28th Cavalry Regiments, the last horse-mounted units in US military history.Following the war, these exact military structures were preserved rather than demolished, transitioning into private ownership in the late 1950s where they were converted into residential apartments and long-term commercial spaces that still stand at the address today, the report said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: BENGALURU: The Karnataka government on Thursday suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, who is facing allegations linked to irregularities in the KPSC recruitment process.Gangwar is currently in CID custody as the agency probes irregularities at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) is separately investigating the case."In exercise of the powers conferred under Rule 3(2) read with 3(3) of the All India Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, IAS (KN: 2016), is placed under suspension with immediate effect and until further orders, pending further investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department," the government order said.During his suspension, the officer will be paid subsistence allowance in accordance with Rule 4 of All India Service (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 1969. serving as director of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) in the Department of Industries and Commerce.The CID is probing allegations of irregularities in the recruitment examination, articles.title: Scientists are using Burmese pythons as ‘living sensors’ as their bodies reveal what’s hiding in Florida’s polluted wetlands
articles.summary: Tech News News: Florida’s Burmese pythons are notorious for swallowing native wildlife, but scientists are finding another use for these invasive snakes. Their bodies.
articles.body: Florida’s Burmese pythons are notorious for swallowing native wildlife, but scientists are finding another use for these invasive snakes. Their bodies can function as biological sensors, carrying chemical traces that reveal what is happening inside the wetlands they inhabit. Researchers are examining python tissues for pollutants including mercury and a class of persistent chemicals known as PFAS, using the snakes to understand contamination across the Greater Everglades ecosystem. A 2026 study led by University of Florida researchers found PFAS in the livers of 67 Burmese pythons, while earlier research has documented mercury accumulation in the species. Because the snakes are already being captured as part of invasive-species removal programmes, scientists can collect samples without deliberately taking additional animals from vulnerable native populations.Why Burmese pythons can act as biological sensorsThe idea rests on the way Burmese pythons live and feed. The species is a long-lived apex predator with a broad diet, meaning an individual snake can consume prey from different parts of the ecosystem and accumulate contaminants that have already moved through the food web. Researchers describe them as holophagous consumers because they swallow their prey whole, potentially taking in the contaminants contained throughout that prey. Their position high in the food chain also means chemicals that accumulate in smaller organisms can become concentrated in their tissues over time. The 2026 PFAS study, led by Lauren E Blackman and colleagues at the University of Florida and partner organisations, argues that these characteristics make Burmese pythons particularly useful as environmental sentinels.Scientists found PFAS inside python liversThe latest evidence comes from the study Invasive Burmese pythons (Python bivittatus) as sentinels for PFAS biomonitoring in the Greater Everglades Ecosystem, published in Science of the Total Environment in May 2026. Researchers examined liver samples from 67 Burmese pythons collected within or near the Greater Everglades ecosystem. The researchers screened the samples for 30 PFAS compounds using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Nine PFAS were quantified above the laboratory limit of quantification. Linear PFOS was particularly widespread, being detected in 93% of the python livers, with a median concentration of 89 nanograms per gram of dry tissue. The median concentration for the combined PFAS measured in the study was 111 nanograms per gram of dry tissue.The snakes carried more PFAS than a native apex predatorThe findings also provided a striking comparison with a native predator. The median total PFAS concentration measured in the Burmese python livers exceeded concentrations reported in livers of American alligators living in the same broader ecosystem. The researchers did not find a statistically significant difference in PFAS concentrations between snakes sampled from eastern and western areas surrounding the Everglades. They did, however, find a strong difference between the sexes. Male pythons had significantly higher combined PFAS concentrations than females, with the reported statistical test producing a p-value below 0.0001. Among females, PFAS concentrations tended to decline as body length and mass increased, which the researchers said could be consistent with maternal transfer of contaminants.Why the findings matter for the EvergladesPFAS, short for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, are a large family of human-made chemicals known for their persistence in the environment. Their presence in wildlife can provide evidence that contaminants are moving through food webs rather than remaining confined to water or sediment. The python study is therefore not simply a survey of chemicals inside individual snakes. It offers a way of examining the broader contaminant burden of the Greater Everglades ecosystem. The researchers argue that using an invasive predator already targeted for removal creates an unusual monitoring opportunity. Instead of capturing additional native wildlife specifically for pollution studies, scientists can make use of animals already being removed as part of management programmes.Mercury tells another pollution storyPFAS are not the first contaminants scientists have tracked through Burmese pythons. Mercury has already established the species as a useful biomonitor in southern Florida. In a 2019 study published in the Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology, Darren G Rumbold of Florida Gulf Coast University and Ian A Bartoszek examined tissues from 227 Burmese pythons captured in southwest Florida between 2012 and 2018. Mercury concentrations reached 4.86 milligrams per kilogram in the liver of one 4.7-metre snake. Across 123 tail-tip samples, the average concentration was 0.12 ± 0.19 milligrams per kilogram. The researchers concluded that snakes could provide an opportunity to monitor mercury at the aquatic-terrestrial interface, particularly because their capture could be combined with invasive-python control efforts.A USGS dataset stretches the picture across two decadesThe evidence has since expanded beyond individual studies. The US Geological Survey released a dataset in 2025 titled Mercury Concentrations in Burmese Pythons Across the Greater Everglades Region in Florida from 2001 to 2022. Scientists examined mercury concentrations in python tail muscle across two major periods, 2001 to 2011 and 2014 to 2019, with snakes sampled across wetland, forested and urban habitats. The work also included tissues from offspring of six female pythons collected in 2022. Kidney, liver and muscle samples from the young snakes were examined to investigate mercury cycling within their bodies, while mercury in maternal blood was assessed to investigate transfer from mothers to offspring.Scientists can read pollution through the food webThe value of using pythons is that their bodies can integrate information that would otherwise require extensive environmental sampling. A water sample provides a snapshot of contamination at one location and one moment. A predator that has travelled through the landscape and consumed multiple prey species can carry a longer biological record of exposure. Scientists can then compare contaminant concentrations with the snake’s location, size, sex and other characteristics to investigate how pollutants are distributed and accumulated. The USGS specifically notes that Burmese pythons accumulate mercury through their consumption of smaller prey containing the metal, making them potentially useful for understanding mercury patterns across the Greater Everglades ecosystem.Invasive snakes offer an unusual research advantageThere is an important practical advantage behind the approach. Burmese pythons are an invasive species in southern Florida and are already the subject of extensive removal programmes because of their impact on native wildlife. Researchers can therefore obtain tissues from captured snakes without creating an additional sampling pressure on threatened or protected native predators. The 2019 mercury study highlighted this point, noting that incorporating contaminant monitoring into python-control work could be cost effective and could reduce concerns about removing native snakes for research. The 2026 PFAS study similarly presents the invasive species as an opportunity to study environmental contamination while supporting existing management efforts.The research could reveal more than one pollutantThe significance of the work extends beyond mercury and PFAS. The same basic principle could potentially be applied to other contaminants that accumulate in wildlife tissues. Researchers are particularly interested in chemicals that persist in ecosystems, move through food webs and accumulate in predators. Because Burmese pythons occupy both aquatic and terrestrial environments and consume a wide range of prey, their tissues can potentially provide information about contamination across ecological boundaries. The 2026 researchers described the species as a suitable sentinel for assessing the broader PFAS burden of the Everglades, building on earlier evidence that pythons can be used to investigate mercury contamination.The snakes are not replacing conventional pollution monitoringCalling Burmese pythons “moving sensors” is useful shorthand, but the scientific method has limits. The snakes do not measure pollution directly and their tissues cannot automatically identify where every contaminant came from. Their diets, movements, age, sex, body size and reproductive status can all influence the concentrations found in their bodies. The PFAS researchers themselves found sex-related differences and possible evidence of maternal transfer, showing why biological measurements have to be interpreted carefully. Python samples are therefore best viewed as one layer of environmental monitoring that can complement measurements of water, sediment, prey and native wildlife.An invasive predator becomes an environmental recordThe research creates an unusual reversal in the story of Florida’s Burmese pythons. The snakes arrived as an invasive species and have become a major ecological problem, but the same characteristics that make them formidable predators also make them valuable scientific subjects. Their long lives, broad diets, position near the top of the food chain and ongoing removal from the Everglades give researchers access to biological evidence of contamination. With PFAS now detected in python livers and decades of mercury data available, scientists are turning an invasive animal into a source of information about the health of the wetland it has invaded. In that sense, each captured python can provide more than evidence of an invasive species problem. Its tissues can also contain a chemical record of the ecosystem through which it has moved.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Israel’s siege on Gaza is forcing dentists to operate in the streets
articles.summary: Scarce resources and office space mean that dental work is a luxury for most people in Gaza.
articles.body:
Dr. Rizq Sufyan Abo Halima operates a dental clinic in Gaza City out of a tent due to the destruction of his previous clinics during Israel's war, facing challenges of high costs and limited supply of properties.

The scarcity of materials and high rent prices in Gaza have forced Dr. Abo Halima to use a tent as a cost-effective alternative for his clinic, allowing him to charge patients less for dental procedures.

Patients in Gaza are faced with difficult choices due to the economic hardships caused by the war, with some opting for tooth extraction over costly fillings as a result of the high prices of dental treatments.

Gaza City, Gaza Strip – In the stifling heat of Gaza City, Dr Rizq Sufyan Abo Halima sits in a small tent pitched in an alleyway, waiting for his next patient.

The tent was a last resort for the doctor, given that the high demand and low supply of properties in the Gaza Strip as a result of Israel's genocidal war have made finding an affordable surgery impossible.

"The stifling rise in temperatures was my first challenge," he told Al Jazeera. "I had to adjust the corners of the tent and lift it at the ends to allow air to pass through."

His old clinic, Smile One, in Sheikh Zayed City in northern Gaza, was bombed during the early days of the war in 2023.

The 31-year-old built a new clinic in May last year, next to where his current tent is pitched, in Gaza City's al-Nasr neighbourhood. But three months later, it too was destroyed when Israeli forces assaulted the area, just weeks before the ceasefire last October.

He is now forced to conduct operations and other emergency dental procedures in the tent close to the ruins of his former surgery. When the electricity supply stops, which is frequent, there is little he can do but sit in his tent and wait for the power to come back on.

Finding another office would be the obvious solution, but residential and commercial units are hard to find in Gaza and those few that remain are unaffordable.

More than four in five buildings in Gaza City and northern Gaza have been completely destroyed or severely damaged in Israel's war, according to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).

Fewer than one in five buildings in Gaza can still be used and Israel's ban on building materials has made repairs impossible. That has created a skewed supply situation, which has made prices of office spaces or homes unaffordable.

"Before the war, I used to rent an entire apartment for my clinic for 500 shekels ($166) a month, but today I cannot afford the prices of remaining apartments at all," he said. Now, the cost is closer to $1,000.

Using a tent is the cheapest alternative Dr Abo Halima could find, and he does not want to pass on what he calls the excessive price of building rent to his customers, who are already suffering immense personal and financial hardships.

"If I had rented an apartment for my clinic instead of a tent, the cost of one filling to teeth would have doubled for the patient," Dr Abo Halima said.

"I am here, enduring the harsh summer heat, so that I can protect people from the high prices that I will inevitably have to charge if I rent an apartment, in addition to the fact that I have no other options at all."

Dr Abo Halima treats his instruments with care. He sterilises them regularly to protect them from dust and germs and hires a security guard. After all, the thin canvas walls offer little protection from thieves.

Despite his best efforts, the collapsed, resource-starved economy in Gaza means that dental care is a luxury for many patients.

One of them, 25-year-old Yousef Abo Halima, sums up the situation in a few simple words: "I can handle the harsh heat inside the tent, but I certainly cannot afford the high costs of fillings at clinics that operate inside apartments".

After Heba Rihan, 23, graduated from Al-Aqsa University with a major in general nursing, she struggled to find work in her field.

So she made an arduous daily journey from the south of the Gaza Strip to the west on foot, looking for work. She eventually found Dr Abo Halima's clinic in May and began working there.

Now, one of the most regular parts of her job is explaining to patients that the high cost of treatment is due to the scarcity of materials and other issues related to the war and Israel's siege on Gaza.

"One day [a patient] came in deep pain… When he asked how much the filling cost and was told it was 350 shekels ($116), he didn't have the money. He asked directly about the tooth extraction, which is only 50 shekels ($17)," she said.

"He decided to extract his original tooth because he could not bear the pain or the cost. That was the most painful moment I've ever had here."

articles.title: In 1964, a couple bought 535 acres in North Carolina and built a summer home there; decades later, they donated the entire property to Great Smoky Mountains National Park in its largest land gift since the park was created
articles.summary: US News: A high-altitude property first bought as a private family retreat in the mid-1960s now serves as an important centre for environmental research in Nor.
articles.body: A high-altitude property first bought as a private family retreat in the mid-1960s now serves as an important centre for environmental research in North America. The 535-acre property in Haywood County, North Carolina, historically known as "The Purchase", was officially transferred to the National Park Service around the turn of the millennium. Former owners Kathryn McNeil and Voit Gilmore donated the land, which became part of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. It was the largest single private land gift to the park since its establishment in 1934. Located along the Cataloochee Divide, the property sits on a high ridge next to the existing national park boundary. Its main landmark is Purchase Knob, a 5,086-foot peak offering wide views of the surrounding mountains.McNeil and Gilmore bought the property in 1964 and built a summer home on the mountain ridge. For almost four decades, the land was used as a quiet family retreat. In 2000, however, the owners decided to give up private ownership permanently to protect the area's high-elevation ecosystems for the future. According to records from the Great Smoky Mountains National Park website, the acquisition added important land to the federal park, which covers more than 520,000 acres across North Carolina and Tennessee. Park officials soon recognised the gift as an important addition to scientific research in the region.A permanent mountain research centreSoon after the land was transferred, the US Congress approved funding to create five specialised research centres across the national park system. In 2001, "The Purchase" was selected as the site of the Appalachian Highlands Science Learning Center. Instead of tearing down the original homes and buildings, the National Park Service adapted them for scientific research. Today, the former summer property includes offices, laboratories, a classroom that can hold 50 people and accommodation for up to eight visiting researchers at a time. The property also contains a preserved historic cabin that provides a glimpse into the area's earlier human history. The learning centre changed the main purpose of the ridge from private recreation to public scientific research. Its location gives researchers direct access to high-elevation environments that are especially sensitive to changes in climate, air pollution and biodiversity. About 5,000 people take part in programmes at the site each year, including scientists, teachers and school students. Research covers many areas of ecology, including changes in tree lines, lichen monitoring, insect studies and air quality.Preserving high-elevation habitatsThe environmental importance of the 535-acre property comes largely from its high and varied landscape. Mountain ridges above 5,000 feet in the Southern Appalachians support rare plants and animals, including species that survived from the last ice age. Before the land was donated, high-elevation areas outside the park faced continued pressure from developers looking to build luxury homes and resorts. By placing the property under federal protection, McNeil and Gilmore helped prevent the forest along the Cataloochee Divide from being broken into smaller sections. Scientists at the Appalachian Highlands Science Learning Center also study species that were not recorded in older park surveys. Through projects such as the All Taxa Biodiversity Inventory, researchers and students have identified thousands of organisms around Purchase Knob and nearby slopes, helping scientists understand the Smokies' complex ecosystems. The centre also gives young students opportunities to take part in scientific work. Field trips allow school groups from the region to collect information alongside professional biologists, giving them practical experience with field sampling and data collection.Legacy of the 2000 land giftThe size of the McNeil and Gilmore donation remains unusual in the modern history of the park. The creation of Great Smoky Mountains National Park in the 1920s and 1930s depended heavily on state funding, private donations and land purchases and condemnations. However, land additions of this size have become rare. More recent additions have generally involved smaller properties secured through conservation agreements or direct purchases by land trusts. In documents describing the history of the Appalachian Highlands Science Learning Center, park officials highlighted the lasting importance of the donation. The National Park Service says staff members and visiting researchers continue to use the facilities that were part of the family's original property. "Every day, the staff and program participants thank the family for their generous gift," the National Park Service says in its historical facility overview. What began as a private mountain property purchased in 1964 eventually became a permanent public resource for high-altitude research. articles.title: Trump proposes stripping tax-exempt status from 18,000 schools over race-based benefits
articles.summary: US News: The Trump administration has proposed stripping private schools, colleges and other educational institutions of their tax-exempt status if they provid.
articles.body: The Trump administration has proposed stripping private schools, colleges and other educational institutions of their tax-exempt status if they provide admissions, scholarships or other benefits to students based on race.The proposed rule, announced by the Treasury Department on Thursday, could affect as many as 18,000 institutions and is part of President Donald Trump’s broader push to eliminate race-based diversity programmes in education, the Associated Press reported.Under the proposal, schools that provide benefits on the basis of race, colour or national or ethnic origin could lose their tax-exempt status. However, the rule would not cover religious institutions or race-neutral considerations such as family income, individual hardship, military family status or academic achievement.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said institutions would not be able to avoid the proposed restrictions simply by changing the language used to describe race-based programmes.“Schools rebranding race-based preferences as equitable, inclusive, or diversity-enhancing does not change their discriminatory nature,” Bessent said.The proposal would apply to private primary and secondary schools, colleges, universities, professional schools and trade schools, including institutions that do not receive federal funding.Schools could face fundraising impactLosing tax-exempt status could have consequences beyond the taxes institutions themselves would have to pay. Donations to tax-exempt organisations are generally eligible for tax deductions, meaning schools could find it harder to attract contributions if donors lose that benefit.The administration has increasingly used federal policies to challenge diversity, equity and inclusion programmes at educational institutions. Trump has also targeted Harvard University in his broader dispute with colleges over what he has described as ideological and antisemitic problems on campuses.The proposed regulations are scheduled to apply to taxable years beginning on or after May 31, 2027, if they are finalised. The proposal will first go through a public comment process and could be modified before becoming final.Supreme Court ruling citedThe Treasury Department cited a 2023 Supreme Court ruling involving Students for Fair Admissions in support of the proposed regulations. The court ruled that colleges could not consider race in admissions decisions under the Equal Protection Clause of the 14th Amendment.The ruling directly concerned admissions, but its impact extended to other areas of higher education, including race-specific scholarships and financial aid programmes.There is also a historical precedent for the government revoking a college’s tax-exempt status. Bob Jones University lost its tax exemption in the 1970s after maintaining a policy banning interracial dating and marriage. The Supreme Court later upheld the IRS decision.Education leaders have criticised the latest proposal, warning it could create additional compliance requirements and uncertainty for colleges while affecting scholarship funding.The administration, however, has described the move as an effort to ensure that educational institutions follow federal civil rights requirements and restore merit-based policies.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Israel releases Lebanese civilian, says five prisoners will be freed
articles.summary: The prisoner, identified as Malek Ghazi, is the first Lebanese citizen held by Israel to be set free since talks began.
articles.body:
Israel has released one Lebanese civilian detainee and has pledged to free five prisoners, the first such handover since the outbreak of the latest Israel-Hezbollah war six months ago.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement on Thursday that Israel agreed to release the Lebanese civilians held by Israeli forces in southern Lebanon after Beirut helped search for the bodies of Lebanese Jewish leaders who were “abducted and murdered by terrorist organisations” in the 1980s.

Netanyahu’s statement added that after being interrogated, the five detainees were found not to be “members of a terrorist organisation” or “involved in terrorism”.

The first released prisoner, identified as Malek Ghazi, was handed over to the Lebanese army via the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), a Lebanese security official said.

Ghazi was handed over to the ICRC at the border crossing in the southern Lebanese coastal town of Naqoura. He was then transferred to a Lebanese army intelligence office in the southern port city of Tyre, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency reported.

Ghazi’s family, hailing from the southeastern town of Ain Ata near the southern border village of Shebaa, said last October that they had lost contact with him after he went out to exercise.

He is the first citizen held by Israel to be released since US-brokered negotiations between Beirut and Tel Aviv began in April .

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam hailed the release in a statement, thanking “the American administration … for the efforts exerted in this regard”.

Salam pledged to continue working “until the release of all our prisoners, the disclosure of the fate of the missing, and the achievement of a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Reports at least 30 people held by Israel

In its last round of negotiations with Israel in August, Lebanon demanded the release of detainees held by Israel since the 2024 war between Israel and Hezbollah, a Lebanese official told the AFP news agency at the time.

Lebanese authorities have not announced the number of citizens held by Israel since 2024, but a list of more than 30 people has been compiled by their families and a committee following up on their cases.

After Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, clashes between the Israeli army and Hezbollah began. This led to over a year of hostilities that escalated into a full-blown war in 2024.

Two years later, Lebanon was fully drawn into the conflict after the US and Israel launched a war on Iran when Hezbollah, a key ally of Iran, fired rockets into Israel in retaliation for the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Israel responded with heavy air strikes and a ground invasion that have killed more than 4,300 people in Lebanon.

Violence has slowed since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding provided for a “ceasefire” in June, followed by an agreement between Israel and Lebanon later that same month.

The Lebanon-Israel deal calls for the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in “pilot zones”.

While another round of talks is expected to take place in Rome later this month, Israel continues to launch attacks across southern Lebanon.

On Thursday, Israeli forces advanced into Halta village in southeastern Lebanon near the border with the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency reported. Israeli drones also flew over the Tyre region at dawn.

Israeli forces also carried out detonations in the south-central towns of Haddatha and Baraachit in Nabatieh governorate and demolished homes in the coastal southern town of al-Mansouri, the news agency reported.

articles.title: US billionaire Leon Black defies summons and sues Epstein panel
articles.summary: The lawsuit calls the House Oversight Committee's subpoenas, which ordered him to share nondisclosure agreements, "invalid".
articles.body:
Billionaire investor Leon Black has failed to appear before a US congressional committee investigating the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein - instead filing a lawsuit challenging the committee's efforts to summon him.

The lawsuit calls the subpoenas issued by the House Oversight Committee "invalid" and says they hold "no legitimate connection" to the committee's legislative aim.

Black walked out of the committee in June while giving voluntary testimony after he was asked about nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) he may have signed, lawmakers said at the time.

Black has denied any wrongdoing with regards to his dealings with Epstein.

The subpoenas, which ordered Black to share NDAs and give an on-camera deposition under oath, were issued after he left the committee meeting in June.

His lawsuit opposing these summonses, which was filed in federal court in Washington on Thursday, argued that revealing the NDAs might "expose women who value their privacy, who have no known or public connection to Epstein, who bargained for confidentiality and have refused to release it".

NDAs are contracts where both parties agree to keep information confidential, often as part of a settlement or employment agreement.

"This is no longer about finding the truth about Epstein. It is about trying to destroy Mr Black," Susan Estrich, an attorney for Black, said in a press release on Thursday.

"We were left with no choice but to file this lawsuit in response to an abuse of Congressional power."

Billionaire Leon Black walks out of Epstein investigation hearing

"By refusing to testify today, Leon Black is now defying two Congressional subpoenas," Robert Garcia, who sits on the committee, said in a statement after Black failed to appear.

"His connections to Epstein and his unwillingness to cooperate are unacceptable. We must hold him in contempt immediately," Garcia added.

Contempt of Congress could result in the committee referring Black to the justice department for potential prosecution.

"It's a shame Leon Black is hiding behind litigation rather than provide answers to the American people," Chairman Jomes Comer said. "Mr Black's testimony is crucial to our investigation."

Black has said he employed Epstein as a wealth management adviser, telling the House Oversight Committee in June that he had paid Epstein $158m (£120m) for legitimate purposes over the course of their years-long association.

He has said he did not know about Epstein's "nefarious activity until Epstein was charged with trafficking in July 2019".

Black appears in the Epstein files released by the justice department, which include photos, videos and investigative documents relating to the disgraced late financier.

There is no suggestion that appearing in the documents implies any wrongdoing.

Black had a six-year affair with a former Russian model, Guzel Ganieva, which ended in allegations of abuse, court records show.

According to a lawsuit filed by Ganieva against Black, which was later dismissed, he prepared a nondisclosure agreement in 2015 to secure her silence.

Epstein offered Black advice, including suggesting in an email to his assistant that Black hire former law enforcement officers to approach Ganieva, according to files released by the US justice department.

Estrich, Black's attorney, has dismissed Ganieva's accusation as "demonstrably false". Black himself has previously said he was the victim of extortion.

A judge ultimately dismissed Ganieva's lawsuit, citing the NDA she signed and about $9m (£6.6m) that she had received in the years after entering the agreement.

Black left Apollo Global Management, a company he co-founded, in 2021 - saying at the time that "relentless public attention and media scrutiny" of his ties with Epstein had taken "a toll" on his health.

articles.title: In 2017, George Lucas bought a 115-hectare French château; he later restored its historic buildings, vineyards, olive groves and surrounding forest
articles.summary: Europe News: In 2017, filmmaker George Lucas acquired Château Margüi, a 115-hectare estate in the Var region of Provence, France, adding it to a small collection o.
articles.body: In 2017, filmmaker George Lucas acquired Château Margüi, a 115-hectare estate in the Var region of Provence, France, adding it to a small collection of properties tied to his Skywalker Vineyards brand. The estate's roots stretch back roughly 2,600 years, when Gallo-Romans first cultivated these very lands near the Argens River, growing wheat, oil, wine, fruits and vegetables on soil fed by many natural springs. The main house, known as the Bastide, was built in 1784 in the traditional style of Aix bastides, featuring a whitewashed facade spanning 600 square metres and 3 floors overlooking a formal French garden below. After decades of change in ownership, including a period of decline during the First World War, the property was bought in 1999, and its vineyards replanted, before Lucas eventually took over and continued restoring its historic buildings, vineyards, olive groves and surrounding forest back to their earlier character.The ancient origins and 18th-century buildings at Château MargüiEvidence of the estate's earliest days emerged in 2002, when archaeologists uncovered remains and amphoras confirming that Gallo-Roman farmers had worked this land beside the Argens River long before written records began. As described in History and estate, the Domaine de Margüi was later run by a family from Aix-en-Provence through the 17th century, before the main Bastide was raised in 1784, complete with a grand staircase leading up to the house and a French garden laid out in front. Additional structures built during this period, including a silk workshop, a sheep pen and a pigeon loft, reflected the working rhythms of a grand Provençal agricultural estate rather than a purely decorative country retreat.Why the estate declined before its 20th century revivalThe First World War brought hardship to Château Margüi, as a shortage of labour combined with a damaging fire left the property weakened for years afterwards. Fortunes turned in the 1920s and 1930s, when melons, apricots, almonds, wheat, grapes and olives once again flourished across the land, echoing the prosperity of centuries past. That golden period eventually faded, and the estate passed through further changes until 1999, when its heiress sold the property to Marie Christine and Philippe Guillanton, who set about relaunching wine production. From the year 2000 onward, they replanted the vineyards, renovated the historic Bastide and added a chapel against its western facade, laying the groundwork for the estate Lucas would later acquire.How George Lucas restored Château Margüi after joining Skywalker VineyardsWhen Château Margüi joined the Skywalker Vineyards collection in 2017, it took its place alongside Lucas's other properties in Marin County, California, and Passignano sul Trasimeno in Italy, all chosen partly for landscapes that echo one another's natural beauty. As detailed in Chateau detail, the estate today comprises 15 hectares of vineyards, 5 hectares of olive trees and 65 hectares of forest, home to century-old conifers and a range of tree species. Under Lucas's direction, restoration work has prioritised Provençal authenticity, transforming historic outbuildings such as the Magnanerie into entertainment spaces while converting other structures into guest suites, a pool house and a clubhouse, all while preserving the essential character of an estate whose story began nearly 3,000 years ago.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Foreign fighters and external support fuel Sudan’s war: UN-backed probe
articles.summary: Investigation says support for warring parties strengthens military capabilities, intensifies humanitarian crisis.
articles.body:
Foreign recruitment and external support networks are sustaining and expanding the civil war in Sudan by providing weapons, military technology and fighters, to the detriment of civilians, according to a United Nations-backed investigation.

A report by the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan, released on Thursday, said transnational entities operating across several countries recruited, trained and deployed foreign personnel to support the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The report also said there were “reasonable grounds to believe” that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) used foreign-supplied drones in its operations that harmed civilians and civilian infrastructure.

Since April 2023, the conflict between the SAF and the RSF has killed tens of thousands of Sudanese and forced millions to flee their homes.

“This support fed into RSF operations in Zamzam camp and later during the takeover of el-Fasher, where the [UN] Mission documented grave human rights and international humanitarian law violations and international crimes, including conduct displaying hallmarks of genocide,” mission member Mona Rishmawi said.

The report said external entities have substantially enhanced the drone capabilities of both the RSF and the SAF, enabling them to strike far beyond front lines.

Documented drone attacks included RSF strikes in Kalogi, South Kordofan that killed 114 people, and army strikes in Ad-Da’ein, East Darfur, which killed at least 70 people and destroyed a major hospital.

Repeated RSF drone strikes in el-Obeid, North Kordofan, especially between July and August this year, may “constitute serious violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, and may amount to war crimes”, the report said.

“The consequences of this external support are being felt most acutely by civilians,” mission chair Mohamed Chande Othman said.

The investigation documented the deployment of up to 2,000 former Colombian military contractors, who it said directly operated combat drones, artillery, and advanced weapons alongside RSF units in Darfur and Kordofan.

The Colombian government told investigators it opposed mercenarism and was taking steps to address the participation of its nationals in foreign conflicts.

Witnesses also reported fighters from South Sudan, Chad and Ethiopia, “including women, serving primarily in frontline, rather than technical roles”, identified by language, accent “and, in some cases uniforms”, the report said.

Private entities, intermediaries and recruiters operating from countries including Colombia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) used transit locations in Chad, Libya and Somalia to facilitate the delivery of personnel, training, weapons and logistics to the RSF in Sudan, the report said.

The UAE rejected allegations that it had provided military, logistical, financial or political support to the RSF. Chad said it remained neutral in the war, and Somalia’s government said it took the report’s allegations seriously, according to the Reuters news agency.

The UN mission urged states to halt illicit supply networks and enforce the UN arms embargo.

Since 2023, Sudan’s civil war has displaced more than 12 million people, devastated civilian infrastructure, collapsed basic services and created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, the UN says. At least three million Sudanese refugees have fled to neighbouring countries including Egypt, Chad and South Sudan.

The UN Human Rights Council established the fact-finding mission in October 2023 to begin gathering evidence of violations in Sudan. The independent investigative team does not speak on behalf of the UN.
